summary_rationale: Uber remains a high-cash-conversion, dual-engine global marketplace compounder, though its 2026 M&A, AV capital, and regulatory complexity require disciplined monitoring. Through Q3 2026, MAPCs reached 215M (+14% YoY), trips reached 4,061M (+16% YoY), Gross Bookings compounded +20% YoY to $59.82B (Q4 guided $63.25B–$65.25B), 9M 2026 GAAP Operating Income rose +39% YoY to $5,260M, and Free Cash Flow hit $7,613M in 9M 2026 ($10.42B TTM, >100% Adjusted EBITDA conversion on 0.6% core capex intensity). Uber One (>50M members) and Advertising (>$2.5B run-rate) continue strengthening unit retention. kpi_health is PASS_WITH_WATCH across six material risks verified through November 2026: (1) autonomous disintermediation and capital intensity as Waymo confirmed ending Austin/Atlanta exclusivity for a standalone app in January 2028 (>500k weekly trips) and Uber committed >$10B across AV equity (~$2.5B) and fleet procurement (~$7.5B, including 35,000+ Lucid/Nuro vehicles); (2) major capital-allocation pivot toward Delivery Hero SE ($14.8B offer, 66.56% tendered in Nov 2026, H2 2027 target close under EC/KFTC/MENA antitrust scrutiny including an Uber-backed SSW Partners carve-out loan) and ezCater ($2.3B), lifting LT debt +49% to $15,664M and slowing Q2–Q3 buybacks; (3) $13,709M insurance reserves requiring $11,372M of restricted cash/investments; (4) multi-jurisdictional tax and labor headwinds including UK HMRC $3.4B back-VAT dispute (~$1.5B Q4 2026 FCF appeal outflow), Nov 4, 2026 High Court of Australia payroll tax loss (>AUD $100M exposure), and the Dec 2, 2026 EU Platform Work Directive transposition deadline; (5) FTC + 21-state federal ROSCA lawsuit targeting Uber One's enrollment/23-screen cancellation flow plus the Oct 2026 FTC algorithmic pricing inquiry; and (6) intensified global Delivery and Mobility competition after DoorDash completed its £2.9B (~$3.9B) Deliveroo acquisition (Oct 2025) alongside Bolt in Europe/Africa and persistently loss-making Freight ($(33)M Q3 loss).
